result.summary: The page is mostly well-formed, but there are a few visual defects: a filter chip is cut off with no visible label, a restaurant name is truncated without ellipsis, and the last pizza card is clipped in a way that hides key information. Overall 4 issues found (2 major, 2 minor).

issues.description: The third restaurant card in 'Fastest near you' shows a truncated name 'Trattoria Piccol' with the text hard-clipped at the screen edge and no ellipsis, making the name unreadable.
issues.suggestion: Apply text truncation with an ellipsis constrained to the card width, or ensure card text wraps within the visible card bounds rather than being clipped by the viewport.

issues.description: The last category filter chip on the right side of the chip row ('All / Pizza / Sushi / Burgers / Healthy / …') is rendered as an almost empty sliver with no visible label, which looks broken rather than like an intentional scroll affordance.
issues.suggestion: Adjust chip spacing/peek amount so the partially visible chip shows at least part of its label, or add a fade/gradient edge to clearly indicate horizontal scrollability.

issues.description: The bottom pizza card in 'Popular right now' is cut off mid-image by the bottom navigation bar, hiding the restaurant name, rating, and delivery info entirely; only the '-20%' badge and heart icon are visible.
issues.suggestion: This may be normal scroll clipping, but consider adding a subtle gradient or ensuring card metadata loads with the card so partially visible cards still convey identity; verify content is reachable on scroll.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' row, the delivery prices are misaligned vertically because the first card's title wraps to one line while others may differ, and the price rows don't share a consistent baseline (e.g., '€0.90 delivery' vs '€2.40 delivery' sit at slightly different visual weights/positions relative to card images).
issues.suggestion: Use a fixed-height title area or align card metadata to a common baseline so prices line up consistently across the carousel.
